target_customer: Patients and families in Indian cities needing emergency or non-emergency ambulance transport
problem: Ambulances in India are slow to arrive and unreliable; HelpNow aimed to cut arrival time with an aggregated ambulance network and cabs converted into first responder MedCabs.
business_model: on-demand ambulance service charging per trip

founders.name: Shikhar Agrawal
founders.background_notes: YC page bio calls him co-founder and Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia.

founders.name: Venkatesh Amrutwar
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio given.

founders.name: Aditya Makkar
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. Press snippets describe the founders as IIT Bombay students or alumni but those pages were not opened.

exit.reason: Cause not public; the YC directory marks the company Inactive.

competitors.name: Ziqitza Healthcare (Dial 108 and 1298)
competitors.what: Large operator of the 108 and 1298 ambulance services, run with state governments
competitors.traction_then: India's second largest ambulance response service per YourStory
competitors.funding_then: Investors include Acumen Fund and HDFC per a later page

technical_complexity.rationale: Dispatch and booking app over a network of partner ambulances; the hard part was operations, driver quality and medical training rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: Aggregating third party ambulances and cabs was copyable by others such as Medulance and Dial4242, which existed in the same period.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals kept operating and a 2021 StanPlus article lists HelpNow among competitors; no acquisition of HelpNow is reported.

market_need_then: Slow ambulance response is a documented problem in Indian cities; coverage in 2020 and 2021 describes HelpNow operating about 12 ambulances in 2019 growing to hundreds and serving COVID patients.

branding.domain_note: Used getHelpNow.in, a prefixed country domain.
branding.brand_signature: MedCabs, rideshare cabs fitted with a mini ambulance kit and trained drivers as first responders.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by several Indian outlets in 2020 and 2021 for COVID era ambulances, including free ambulances run by IIT Bombay students and alumni.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear name and a distinctive MedCabs idea with regional press, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: HelpNow built an on-demand ambulance network in Mumbai and later other cities, grew to a team of about 50 per the YC page, and got coverage during COVID. Funding found is small and rests on aggregators, and no shutdown reporting or founder post-mortem was found, so the cause of going inactive is not public and failure factors are left empty. Ambulance operations are capital and operations heavy, but no source states that as the reason.
notes: Website getHelpNow.in returned HTTP 404 on the fetch. Funding conflicts: FundedIQ lists one undisclosed round of about $200K in March 2020; CB Insights lists $150K over three rounds; a founder interview quoted in a directory mentions 10 lakh INR angel funding early on. The recorded round rests on a single aggregator. Investor Y Combinator is assumed only from the batch; not stated by FundedIQ. Competitors: Medulance (launched 2017) and Dial4242 appear in search results only on undated pages or on a June 2021 StanPlus article that is too late for the 2020 batch, so they are not listed. Cause of inactivity not public.
